catd10.hypothesis: Newly mapped faults are mostly new geometry of existing systems, so the number of new-fault pixels per km^2 tracks the density of already-mapped structure. R0 spreads one dot every ~3 px uniformly over the H19-5 ridge mask, which carries 0.41 dots per km^2-scale block regardless of how much known structure the block holds; moving 10% of the dots from the lowest-density 1 km blocks to the highest raises kernel credit where truth pixels are most numerous.
catd10.mechanism: DTI = T / (0.2T + 0.2(S-M) + 0.8|G|) at fixed S. Moving a dot from a block with near-zero known-structure density to one with 3x the regional density raises the expected max-kernel credit it earns (k(d) = 1 - d/3) and simultaneously raises M, shrinking the wasted-mass term S-M. Both terms push the ratio up; no dot count, mass, spacing or catalogue-distance invariant changes.
catd10.non_fault_mimic: Mapping effort: the catalogue is denser where access, exposure and basin-hosted basin-range normal faults made 1:250k-1:24k compilation easy, not necessarily where 2020s geothermal-focused mapping found new faults. If new truth is instead concentrated in poorly mapped uplands (lidar/surface-imaging targets), this prior is anti-correlated with truth and the variant loses.
catd10.falsifier: A live receipt delta <= -0.01 vs R0 falsifies the known-structure-density prior at 1 km and says the catalogue is a mapping-effort artefact; |delta| < 0.01 is no evidence either way (public chunks only).

phys10.hypothesis: Where magnetic horizontal gradient, isostatic-gravity slope and detrended-elevation slope are jointly high, the crust is more intensely broken per km^2, so truth density per km^2 is high there. This prior is built only from physics, so unlike the catalogue prior it cannot inherit mapping effort or exposure bias.
phys10.mechanism: Same fixed-S budget trade as catd10, with the block prior replaced by the 0.40 pct(tmi_hg) + 0.35 pct(iso_grav_anom_slope) + 0.25 pct(det_elev_slope) mix smoothed to 1 km. Differences ONLY which blocks are donors and receivers: same count, same mass, same spacing floor, same catalogue clearance.
phys10.non_fault_mimic: The same bands respond to non-tectonic contrasts: Tertiary volcanic flow margins, caldera ring fractures, pluton contacts, and lithologic scarps in resistant tuff. Because the physics mix is also what the H19-5 ridge mask was built to track, the implied redistribution is the mildest of the three variants.
phys10.falsifier: If phys10 and catd10 are both negative by >= 0.01 while their implied redistributions are near-disjoint, the axis itself (km-scale reallocation) is wrong, not just the prior.

catdS10.hypothesis: Mirror image of catd10, built because the previous session's IRREGULARITIES entry requires both directions before a CONCENTRATION result can be read as a sign. It moves the same 10% of dots between the same 1 km blocks in the opposite direction, so a monotone (catd10 > R0 > catdS10) or inverted (catdS10 > R0 > catd10) response identifies the sign of the catalogue-density prior; a flat response on both sides says the metric is insensitive to km-scale reallocation at this count.
catdS10.mechanism: Same fixed-S bookkeeping as catd10 with donor and receiver block sets swapped. If the known-structure-density prior is informative, this variant must LOSE: it takes the most truth-dense dots away and re-places them where known structure is absent. Its predicted loss is therefore as informative as catd10's predicted gain.
catdS10.non_fault_mimic: If new-fault truth is genuinely concentrated AWAY from mapped structure (poorly exposed basins, young volcanic terrain, areas no compiler has mapped), this mirror variant wins and catd10 loses — the same evidence, opposite conclusion.
catdS10.falsifier: catdS10 >= catd10 + 0.01 falsifies the known-structure-density prior outright. Both arms within 0.01 of R0 means the axis is inert at 10% and should not be spent on again at this dose.
